questions.question: Explain why and where the first farmers settled in southern Africa.
questions.expected_answer: They settled in the eastern half of southern Africa, because their crops, sorghum and millet, need summer rain, which falls mainly in the east. They chose places near rivers and streams, with good soil, grazing for cattle, wood for building and fuel, and iron ore, often on the slopes of river valleys.

questions.question: Describe the first farmers' attitude to land.
questions.expected_answer: Land belonged to the whole community and was not bought or sold. The chief looked after it on behalf of the people. Every family had the right to use land for a home, fields and grazing, given out by the headman or chief after talking with the elders. Grazing land was shared, and land was linked to the ancestors buried there.

questions.question: How did the first farmers care for the land?
questions.expected_answer: They let old fields rest after some years so the soil could recover, clearing new fields nearby; they moved cattle to different grazing areas so the grass was not eaten to the roots; and when wood and good soil ran out after many years, the village might move.
